title: The Crow and the Pitcher
text:
In a dry season a crow was nearly dying of thirst. Flying over the fields, she spotted a pitcher standing on the ground and swooped down to it, hoping for water.

There was water inside, but only a little, lying at the very bottom. The neck of the pitcher was narrow and the water was low, and however far she pushed her head in and stretched her beak, she could not reach it. She tried to tip the pitcher over, but it was too heavy for her to move.

She was close to giving up when she noticed the small pebbles scattered on the ground nearby. She picked one up in her beak and dropped it into the pitcher. Then she brought another, and another. With each stone, the water rose a little.

It was slow work, and she was tired and parched, but she did not stop. Pebble by pebble, the water climbed up the inside of the pitcher, until at last it came within reach of her beak. The crow drank her fill and flew away.
lesson: When force does not work, look at what is lying around you. Patient, small steps applied with a bit of thought can solve a problem that seemed impossible.
